subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) \u0004 hosted vs current provider \u0004 post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finlytics.com>, Rahul Mehta <rahul.mehta@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99)  hosted vs current provider  post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Rahul 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from Redwood's side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth heading into the validation run.

What we covered (scope):
- Goal: end-to-end p95 / p99 latency qualification for your text-generation path (single-turn, up to 512 tokens) comparing your current provider to Redwood hosted.
- Agreed qualification targets (initial ask): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms (end-to-end, client-observed).
- Workload notes: streaming clients supported (incremental tokens), average response ~220 tokens, peak payload size up to 512 tokens, concurrent active streams target ~100, baseline throughput ~200 qps.
- Important caveats: cold-start vs warm-cache behavior, throughput bursts, and batching effects on p95/p99. We'll record traces for both sides.

Action items / next steps:
1) FinLytics: please share the last 7 days of p95/p99 metrics, percentiles by payload size, and any available traces or flamegraphs (attachment or S3).
2) Redwood: we'll run a hosted smoke/validation run using your sample payloads and the schedule below; we'll share raw traces, token-level timelines, and aggregated p95/p99 across runs.
3) Both: confirm whether streaming should be measured as "time-to-first-token" vs "time-to-last-token" for p95/p99 (we recommend focusing on time-to-first-token for interactive UX, and time-to-last-token for throughput tradeoffs).

Proposed schedule: Redwood runs validation on Sep 3, 09:0012:00 PT (we can shift if that window conflicts).

Attachments: 20270830-finlytics-slo-notes.pdf (summary notes from today).

Questions for you: can you provide a test API key (or a short-lived key) and the procurement contact for any formal approvals? Also confirm the model family (e.g., GPT-like vs LLaMA-family variant) and whether there are per-request hooks or server-side pre/post processing we should be aware of.

Thanks  will coordinate tickets and test plan once we have the data.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99)  hosted vs current provider  post-call recap & next steps

Laura / team 

Thanks for the clear notes, appreciate the recap. Attaching our exported latency data from the current provider for the past 7 days (by payload-size bucket). You'll see p95/p99 broken out; our team is most focused on time-to-first-token for conversational UX.

A few quick answers:
- Model family: a mixture of a tuned open LLM and a smaller reranker for some flows; primary generation model is a 16B variant.
- Average response token length: ~220 tokens; tail workloads up to 512 tokens.
- Server-side pre/post processing: we have an enrichment step (adds ~20ms average) and a synchronous reranker step for certain flows.

Attached: finlytics-currentprovider-latency.csv

We can provide a short-lived API key for the Sep 3 window. Procurement contact: procurement@finlytics.com (cc'ing Rahul).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99)  hosted vs current provider  post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sam 

Thanks for the CSV and the model details  super helpful. Couple of technical clarifications from the infra/serving side to make sure our tests are apples-to-apples: 

- Streaming semantics: do you treat streaming as sending incremental tokens as soon as they're produced (time-to-first-token important), or do you buffer N tokens server-side before emitting chunks? If the latter, please indicate chunk size / buffering window.
- Measurement labeling: can you confirm whether your "p95/p99" in the CSV is measured at the client (end-to-end) or at the provider edge (post-routing)? We need end-to-end client-observed numbers for parity.
- Cold vs warm: any observable cold-start events in the past week (significantly higher latency after idle periods)?
- Max concurrency and connection limits for your current provider (per-tenant)?
- Are you open to Redwood running both streaming-first-token and full-response (last-token) measurements so we can compare both UX and throughput tradeoffs?

We're putting the validation plan in a shared folder here: https://drive.google.com/finlytics-redwood-perf-plan  it includes sample payloads, test harness, and the exact telemetry we will capture (token timelines, per-request spans, and aggregated percentiles).

We recommend we focus the initial pass on time-to-first-token p95/p99, and then run a follow-up pass for time-to-last-token to observe end-to-end throughput effects.

Sam / Rahul 

Great  thanks for the CSV and procurement contact. We're confirmed to run the primary validation pass on Sep 3, 09:0012:00 PT. Plan:
- Run hosted validation in our us-west-2 test environment (we'll pin to a warm pool to minimize cold-start noise).
- Measure both time-to-first-token (primary) and time-to-last-token (secondary).
- We'll run repeats at 50, 100, and 200 qps, and at 50 / 100 concurrent streams, with three 10-minute steady-state windows per condition.

Please provide the short-lived API key (or give us an endpoint and credentials) and confirm that the procurement contact (procurement@finlytics.com) is OK to approve any needed short-term access. If that works, we'll also open a scoped DocuSign for the FIN-2345 PO and include the validation run notes. Link to the DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/finlytics/FIN-2345

If you need to adjust the window, say so by EOD tomorrow and we'll reschedule.

Best,
Laura Bennett
